correctness.rationale: Primary Lemma 4.4 gives the exact legal first/interior/last block ranges. The defect is the sum of the block binomial costs; the geometric-series generating function and coefficient extraction follow by independent choices. For odd n=2m+1 >=11, the coefficients at three consecutive degrees are m-1,m-2,(m-2)(m-3), strictly valleyed. For even n=2m>=14, the coefficients are C(m-2,2),C(m-3,2),2C(m-3,3), again a strict valley. Every remaining n is explicitly evaluated and n=12 is unimodal. Literal brute maximality checks cover n=2..7, with three computation routes to n=27; finite checks supplement, not replace, the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The 2026 maximal-Lehmer-code paper proves the block classification, total Padovan number, and extremal inversion weights but not the exact coefficient-shape dichotomy. The current sharp non-unimodality theorem is proved by new explicit coefficient extraction and uniform strict valleys, rather than reasserting the source classification. No equivalent statement was found in actual targeted source/alias searches; unresolved priority is recorded.
residual_risks: A historically earlier equivalent defect-graded maximal-independent-set or Padovan polynomial shape theorem could exist under different terminology; searches are not proofs of priority.

The weighted generating function is a fairly direct consequence of the source block classification and is not independently novel; the claim of additional value is confined to the sharp infinite coefficient-shape boundary.

The 2024 weighted Padovan paper was compared by its public abstract rather than complete full text; its graph-invariant thesis does not indicate direct coverage. The 2026-07 different-vincular-pattern paper was inspected in relevant open-access sections.

value.rationale: It determines the complete sharp all-length unimodality boundary of a natural inversion-statistic distribution motivated directly by a current Padovan maximal-code enumeration. The loss at 11, recovery at 12, and permanent strict valleys from 13 onward form a structural coefficient phenomenon, not a routine restatement of a minimum or total count; the proof supplies uniform explicit coefficient inequalities.
